quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help a helmet protect you?

options.text: It has no cracks or damage.

questions.explanation: A helmet protects you best when it meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly, and has no damage like cracks or loose padding.

questions.question: What should passengers do?

options.text: Look over the rider's shoulder when turning.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over the rider's shoulder when turning.
questions.explanation: Passengers should look over the rider's shoulder in the direction of any turn. This helps the rider and motorcycle lean the right way.

questions.question: Your motorcycle is weaving on a metal bridge grating. What should you do?

options.text: Downshift to a lower gear immediately.
Ride in a zigzag pattern across the bridge.

questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves on bridge gratings, stay relaxed and go straight at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than the weaving.

questions.question: Which lane position makes a motorcycle easiest to see?
questions.explanation: Ride in the center lane position when you can. This puts you in the driver's rearview mirror so they can see you.

questions.question: When reacting to a road hazard, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Use your horn, lights, or signals.

questions.explanation: Use your horn, lights, and signals to tell other drivers you are there. Adjust your speed and position as needed.

questions.question: Before you start riding, the fuel valve should be:
questions.explanation: Open the fuel valve before you ride. If it is closed, the engine will start but stall once the fuel in the lines runs out.

questions.question: Is it good to use all three lane positions?

options.text: No, because you will not get used to any part of the lane.
No, because it confuses other drivers.
Yes, if road and traffic conditions change.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if road and traffic conditions change.
questions.explanation: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions. No single position is always best.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a car on the left, ride in which part of the lane?
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane when passing. This gives you a better view and signals to other drivers that you are passing.

questions.question: Why should a motorcyclist change gears before turning?

options.text: To avoid a sudden power change in the middle of the turn.
To keep both hands on the handlebars during the turn.
To prevent the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: To avoid a sudden power change in the middle of the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you turn. Shifting during a turn can cause sudden power changes that make the rear wheel skid.

questions.question: A motorcycle horn is ________ a car horn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle horn is not as loud as a car horn. Use it when needed, but do not rely on it to stay safe.

questions.question: When riding in a group and entering a curve, what formation should you use?
questions.explanation: Groups normally ride in a staggered formation. Switch to single-file when taking a curve, making a turn, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when entering a curve?

options.text: Wherever traffic and road conditions require

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever traffic and road conditions require
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose your lane position based on current conditions and adjust as needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How quickly the alcohol is consumed
How often the person consumes alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the person consumes alcohol
questions.explanation: BAC is determined by body weight, the amount of alcohol consumed, and how quickly it was consumed. Never ride after drinking alcohol.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should maintain?
questions.explanation: Keep at least three seconds between you and the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. Increase this distance if conditions are poor.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that the road ahead will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: When someone is passing you from behind, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is the safest position when being passed. Riding near the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding on the far side may cause the driver to return to your lane too early.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When someone is following you too closely
When you will be slowing down suddenly
When there is a stop sign ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will be slowing down suddenly
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is not as visible as a car's. Flash your brake light when slowing or stopping so others notice you are slowing down. This is especially important when slowing faster than expected.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They show traffic laws for that area. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes together when the rear brake is applied
It automatically applies the brake based on your riding habits
It applies the brake when you downshift

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes together when the rear brake is applied
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems that link the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake pedal. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's brakes.

questions.question: When someone is passing you on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when someone is passing you on the left. Riding on the right side can be dangerous. It may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: _________ of motorcycle and car collisions happen because the car driver did not yield to the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle and car collisions happen because car drivers fail to yield the right-of-way. Never assume that larger vehicles will yield to you, even if they are supposed to by law.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what is correct?

options.text: You can go faster than the speed limit while passing.
You can pass in a no-passing zone if you started in a passing zone.
You must follow the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must follow the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: Always follow the posted speed limit while passing. You can only pass in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Stop only if other traffic is coming.
Vehicles will enter the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, let all traffic and pedestrians pass, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When a passenger rides on your motorcycle, you should tell them to:

options.text: Get on before you start the engine.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.explanation: Tell passengers to avoid talking or moving while the motorcycle is moving. Passengers should only get on after you start the engine. They should sit as far forward as possible without bothering you.
